## 1. The kindled fire and the cloudburst  (`#the-fire-and-the-cloudburst`)

Cited ayat: 2:17-20

> **2:17** مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِى ظُلُمَٰتٍ لَّا يُبْصِرُونَ
>
> **2:18** صُمٌّۢ بُكْمٌ عُمْىٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
>
> **2:19** أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَٰتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَٰبِعَهُمْ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلْمَوْتِ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطٌۢ بِٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
>
> **2:20** يَكَادُ ٱلْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَٰرَهُمْ كُلَّمَآ أَضَآءَ لَهُم مَّشَوْا۟ فِيهِ وَإِذَآ أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا۟ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَٰرِهِمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

### Claims

**c1** (2:17): The ayah says that their similitude is that of one who kindled a fire; when it lit up what was around him, God took away their light and left them in darknesses, unable to see.

**c2** (2:18): They are deaf, dumb and blind, so they do not return.

**c3** (2:19): The ayah then gives another picture, introduced by the word or: a cloudburst from the sky with darknesses, thunder and lightning in it, from whose thunderclaps they try to shut themselves away for fear of death, while God encompasses the disbelievers.

**c4** (2:20): The lightning almost snatches away their sight; whenever it lights up for them they walk in it, and when it grows dark on them they stand still, and had God willed He would have taken away their hearing and their sight, for God has power over all things.

### One-minute summary

The ayat give a picture of one who kindled a fire, whose light God took away and who was left in darknesses, and another of a cloudburst with darknesses, thunder and lightning [c1][c3]. In the picture of the cloudburst they walk when the lightning lights up for them and stand still when it grows dark [c4].

### Complete story

The ayah says that their similitude is that of one who kindled a fire [c1]. When it lit up what was around him, God took away their light and left them in darknesses, unable to see [c1]. They are deaf, dumb and blind, so they do not return [c2].

The ayah then gives another picture, introduced by the word or [c3]. It is a cloudburst from the sky with darknesses, thunder and lightning in it, and they try to shut themselves away from its thunderclaps for fear of death, while God encompasses the disbelievers [c3]. The lightning almost snatches away their sight [c4]. Whenever it lights up for them they walk in it, and when it grows dark on them they stand still [c4]. Had God willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight, for God has power over all things [c4].

### Deep study

The pictures are joined by the word or, and the ayat do not say whether it presents an alternative or a further description of the same people [c3]. In the picture of the fire the light comes from a kindled fire and is taken away, and in the picture of the cloudburst it comes from the lightning and comes and goes [c1][c4]. The ayat call the people deaf, dumb and blind, and the closing ayah says that God could have taken away their hearing and their sight [c2][c4].

### Kids mode

A person kindled a fire, and it lit up what was around him [c1]. Then God took away their light and left them in darknesses [c1]. The next picture is a cloudburst with darkness, thunder and lightning [c3]. When the lightning lights up, they walk, and when it grows dark, they stand still [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the picture of the fire turns on light being given and then taken away [c1]. Another reading is that the picture of the cloudburst shows the same people walking when it is light and standing still when it is dark [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the pronoun their points to in 2:17; it refers to people described in ayat before 2:17, which are outside the ayat cited for this item.
- Not established: what the kindled fire and the cloudburst stand for beyond what the ayat themselves say about the people.
- The ayah itself uses the word for a similitude (mathal) in the picture of the fire.
- The sense of the word or (aw) in 2:19 is read as an alternative or as an addition; this draft leaves it open.
- The Arabic of 2:19 also names what they put against the thunderclaps, and it is a part of the body; this draft says only that they shut themselves away.
